prompts.title: Slow Push-In on the Existing Football Scene
prompts.prompt: Animate the supplied football input image as the single reference for 6 seconds of hyperrealistic vertical 9:16 footage. The camera performs one slow, continuous push-in toward the existing subject, easing gently to a stop near the end. Movement stays small enough that no new area of the scene is invented. Keep all original people, kits, colours, crests and flags exactly as shown, with stable anatomy and legible faces. Allow only restrained, physically plausible life the image supports: quiet breathing, fabric settling, grass stirring, and a slight ball or limb shift if clearly visible. Leave the lower frame open and uncluttered for subtitles. Do not add players, events, scores, statistics or identities. No generated text, narration or music.

prompts.prompt: From the supplied football input image, build 6 seconds of hyperrealistic vertical 9:16 motion. The camera tracks smoothly sideways at a constant speed, producing only a small shift in viewpoint and restrained foreground-to-background parallax, then holds steady. Because the reference is a single frame, keep the lateral travel modest so no unseen area, stand or stadium detail is revealed. Preserve every original person, kit, crest, flag and colour, with stable anatomy and clearly readable faces. Add only coherent sports motion the image supports: a foot planting, a torso turning slightly, a ball rolling a short distance. Keep the lower frame free for subtitles. Do not invent players, events, scores or identities. No text, narration or music.

prompts.title: Rack Focus Between Existing Subjects
prompts.prompt: Animate the supplied football input image for 6 seconds of hyperrealistic vertical 9:16 footage. The camera repositions only slightly while performing one smooth rack focus, shifting sharpness from one existing subject or plane in the frame to another and settling there, keeping both inside the same unchanged football setting. Depth of field changes convincingly with no morphing, warping or doubled anatomy. Preserve all original people, kits, colours, crests and flags, and keep faces legible, with small coherent movements such as breathing, a slight turn of the shoulders or a short ball roll where visible.
